items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: John Hammond, who was my producer, liked very much the idea of recognizable tunes plus originals.

ctx.x: When you do a recording, in the old days an LP and now CDs, the people you’re working with, either producers or record companies, do they like to see well-known tunes on the recordings as well as your own material?

I think that’s varied over the years, Monk. Like when I first started recording for Columbia back in the early ‘60s, John Hammond, who was my producer, liked very much the idea of recognizable tunes plus originals. And that’s not an unusual stance for a producer to take. But over the years I’ve had projects where I’ve done albums totally of original compositions and albums all of standards, and I think it really depends on the record label, what their predilection is at the moment. I generally like to do mixtures…
is wonderful but sometimes it’s a little harder for the listener to get into. So having an album that has a balance of the two often I think is the best way to go.
